newsitem.title: USA: Pepsico board approves restaurant spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Pepsico board approves restaurant spin-off.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc said on Thursday that its board approved the spin-off of its restaurant business, which include KFC, Taco Bell and Pizza Hut, to shareholders.
Under the plan, the separation of Pepsi's restaurant business from its beverage and Frito-Lay snack foods business will occur at the end of the day on October 6, 1997.

Shareholders of record on September 19, 1997 will receive one share in the new restaurant company, which is called TRICON Global Restaurants Inc, for every 10 shares of Pepsi common stock, Pepsi said in a statement.

Pepsi said the board approved a plan requiring TRICON, which has about $10 billion in annual revenues, to enter into separate financing arrangements and to pay Pepsi a $4.5 billion one-time distribution at the time of the spin off.
Proceeds from this one-time distribution will be used to repay PepsiCo debt and repurchase shares, Pepsi said.
Completion of the spinoff is subject to clearance by the Securities and Exchange Commission, Pepsi said.
